evals.name: mixed registry preserves public facade
evals.prompt: Our Rust streams.rs is 3,900 lines: 1,600 lines of stream tables, about 500 of schema/host discovery/limits/lookups, and 1,600 of tests and a witness table. Reorganize it without changing example_config::streams::* callers.
expectations: Separate declarative registry data from substantial schema and runtime responsibilities
Keep host discovery and geometry rules in cohesive named modules rather than a leftovers helper file
Keep a facade with explicit re-exports preserving existing public paths and type identity
Move bulky tests and witness data behind cfg(test) without exposing production internals
Validate unchanged values, ordering, feature gates, and affected downstream compilation

evals.name: coherent long table is not a defect by count
evals.prompt: This 1,200-line Rust file is a coherent declarative opcode table with a tiny lookup. Split it into files below 500 lines unless that makes maintenance worse; there is no project line limit.
expectations: Treat the numeric size as an inspection signal rather than a universal limit
Keep the coherent table and its small lookup together if no semantic partition improves navigation
Do not create numbered chunks or one file per opcode

evals.name: short mixed file still warrants a boundary
evals.prompt: A 280-line Rust module mixes CLI argument parsing, database retry policy, and a binary wire decoder. We are extending the decoder; suggest its source layout.
expectations: Choose boundaries by responsibility despite the low total line count
Inspect callers and shared invariants before proposing the decoder's home
Keep the requested change scoped rather than forcing an unrelated subsystem redesign

evals.name: small bug fix stays scoped
evals.prompt: Fix one comparison in a 2,500-line Rust module; the module has unrelated organization problems, but I only want the bug fix.
expectations: Honor the narrow fix and avoid a broad file reorganization
Mention a concrete layout concern separately only if useful
Do not make skill use a prerequisite for unrelated cleanup

evals.name: unsafe protocol stays understandable
evals.prompt: This ring-buffer module exceeds 500 production lines. Its atomic ordering, unsafe accesses, and lifetime rules implement one protocol. Should each impl and unsafe helper be moved to its own file?
expectations: Keep the correctness-critical protocol visible together when fragmentation would hide its invariant
Consider independent adapters or bulky test data as safer boundaries
Do not widen visibility or add one-file-per-type modules to hit a numeric target

evals.name: private unit tests remain private
evals.prompt: Move 1,500 lines of unit tests out of src/cache.rs. They use private internals and include a large fixture by relative path. Put them under the crate's top-level tests directory?
expectations: Prefer a cfg(test) child module for tests requiring private internals
Keep the fixture test-only and correct its relative include path
Reserve crate-level integration tests for the public API
Do not make private implementation items public for the move

evals.name: feature-gated facade retains consumers
evals.prompt: Split a public Rust module whose types are re-exported downstream under two platform features. The default unit tests pass after the move. Is that enough?
expectations: Preserve feature and platform gates on moved definitions and facade re-exports
Check relevant supported feature configurations and downstream users
Report unavailable targets as a validation limit rather than claiming coverage

evals.name: generated source excluded from mechanical splitting
evals.prompt: A generated protobuf Rust file is 8,000 lines. Make all Rust source files small without changing the generator or vendored code.
expectations: Do not hand-edit generated output or vendored files
Explain the ownership boundary and leave generated code intact
Keep the skill focused on maintainable handwritten source rather than a blanket size gate
